title: The explicit pro-etale tensor pullback comparison preserves composite adjunction units
statement:
Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes, with the small pro-etale sites, base-change functors $B_f$ and inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use compatible small skeletons as in that definition. Let $R_V,R_W,R_Z$ be sheaves of commutative rings on the respective sites and fix ring-sheaf isomorphisms $c_k:k^{-1}R_V\xrightarrow{\sim}R_W$ and $c_h:h^{-1}R_W\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Z$. Let $a_{h,k}:h^{-1}k^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(k\circ h)^{-1}$ be the inverse-image composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], transported along the canonical fibre-product isomorphisms $q_U:B_hB_kU\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{k\circ h}U$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use its induced comparison on ring sheaves, and set $c_{k\circ h}=c_h\circ h^{-1}(c_k)\circ(a_{h,k,R_V})^{-1}$.

Write $f^*M=f^{-1}M\otimes_{f^{-1}R_{\mathrm{target}},c_f}R_{\mathrm{source}}$ for the module pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Form the explicit tensor comparison $t_{h,k}:h^*k^*\to(k\circ h)^*$ by applying $a_{h,k}$ to the inverse-image factor and multiplying the intermediate scalar into the final scalar. More precisely, on local tensor generators, after the canonical inverse-image and tensor identifications (inverse image commutes with $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ and with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], hence with relative tensor products, which are coequalizers of $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$), it sends $(m\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $m\otimes c_h(a)b$; here $m$ is a local section of $h^{-1}k^{-1}M$, $a$ a local section of $h^{-1}R_W$, and $b$ a local section of $R_Z$. Its inverse sends $m\otimes b$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes b$, using $a_{h,k}^{-1}$ on $m$.

Then these local formulas give mutually inverse natural module-sheaf maps, and this explicit comparison is compatible with the specified adjunctions, not just an unspecified isomorphism of their underlying functors. Precisely, let $d_{h,k}:(k\circ h)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}k_*h_*$ be restriction along $q_U$ on sections (with the module actions induced by the specified coefficient maps), and let $\eta^f$ be the unit of $f^*\dashv f_*$. For every $R_V$-module sheaf $M$,
$$
 k_*h_*(t_{h,k,M})\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*M})\circ\eta^k_M
 =d_{h,k,(k\circ h)^*M}\circ\eta^{k\circ h}_M.
$$
Thus $t_{h,k}$ is the unique left-adjoint comparison corresponding to $d_{h,k}$ under [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] and the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction].

proof.text: Use the existing real-data proEtaleRingInverseImageComp, which is the inverse mate of the fibre-product pushforward comparison. Apply unit_conjugateEquiv_symm to the sheaf adjunctions. Substitute the prescribed composite coefficient identification, commute the pushforward comparison through the coefficient maps by naturality, and cancel its inverse. Naturality of the h-unit with c_k identifies the result with rho_k followed by k_*(rho_h). This proves coefficient_comp.

proof.text: Forget the coefficient compatibility to RingCat. SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr₂ applied to the inverse of the canonical pullbackComp isomorphism, followed by pushforwardComp, gives d from composite direct image to successive direct image. Its component on every section is definitionally restriction along pullbackComp.inv. Let t be the inverse conjugateIsoEquiv image of d for the composite and iterated module adjunctions. unit_conjugateEquiv_symm supplies the required composite-unit equation.

proof.text: Evaluate the unit equation at every U and m. Expand the two tensor generators as scalar multiples of restrictions of module units. The h-unit is linear through rho_h, commutes with restrictions, and t is linear and commutes with restrictions. Move both scalars outside t, commute t through the q and B_h(p) restrictions, and apply the evaluated unit equation. Composing the three restrictions and multiplying the two scalars proves the forward formula. Specialize this formula to T=B_k(U), p=id, the outer index p followed by pullbackComp.hom, and intermediate scalar 1. Ring maps preserve 1 and pullbackComp.hom followed by its inverse is the identity, so applying t.inv and cancelling t.hom proves the inverse formula. Finally equality of the transposes under the iterated adjunction homEquiv proves uniqueness of every component and hence of the natural transformation.

lean.note: Both tensor directions are specified on every inverse-image colimit generator, with arbitrary test objects, indexing arrows and local scalars; universal colimit and sheafification maps make these equivalent to the stated local formulas. The specified tensor-normalized module adjunction is used throughout. The five conclusion clauses specify restriction along q, the forward and inverse tensor formulas, the displayed composite-unit equation, and uniqueness among all natural transformations. c_hk and hc_hk name precisely the prescribed composite coefficient identification. The added landed statement dependency supplies only the existing real-data ring inverse-image composition mate, which has no finiteness hypothesis; no profinite specialization is imposed.
